Full Metal Schoolgirl - 100% Completion Review
Score: 6/10

Full Metal Schoolgirl is a Arcade Roguelike game where you climb a corrupt CEO's tower of 100 floors with a live streaming cyborg girl to avenge their father, after fully completing the game i'll give some pro's, neutrals and cons.

PRO'S:
-Well designed characters that are well designed and stylish
-Good music and soundtrack that suits this type of arcade game well
-Having each run be livestreamed to fans was a pretty unique idea, certainly makes the atmosphere more positive and cheery
-Good combat with lots of different types of weapons and passive ability mods to choose from
-Has a drone that follows your around that can help you out in combat and changed to do different things
-Good amount of body upgrades to make your character stronger and make each run a bit easier
-Good amount of x-appeal, doesn't shy away from the spice
-Has a endless mode once you complete the story and a new game+ mechanic that let's you keep all your stats and body enhancements and play as a different character
-Good boss designs that are each unique and well designed
-Fully voice acted
-Perfect performance, no lag, crashes, glitches or bugs

NEUTRAL'S: "No Score Change From These"
-Game length for full completion about 12-15 hours, depends on luck, rng of course
-No co-op if your wondering, it's purely single player
-Story is your standard Good vs Evil plot

CON'S:
-Key cards for elevators can only be used once, so if you die and you don't have a keycard you have to start over from a lower floor or from the beginning
-Very limited enemy designs, it's pretty much the same enemies in different colors and costumes
-When starting from the elevator you only get a choice of 3 pure rng items, if you don't get anything good your boned
-Can't switch characters, once you choose a character your locked in until you beat the main story, and the 3rd unlockable character can only be acquired in endless mode after the main story
-Can't map any buttons to the mouse buttons, so it's either use a controller or make do with keyboard controls
-Passive abilities mods always have a negative attached to them which is frustrating
-No way to remove some of the rng from the game, such as removing certain weapons, drones or mods from spawning
-Drone has to be constantly activated every 5 - 15 seconds which gets really old, really fast, wish they would have done what Nier Automata did and simply have them on all the time
-Final boss is absurd, 3 stages and huge amount of hp, it's not impossible or overly difficult, just grindy

Overall Full Metal Schoolgirl is a ok arcade game, it's a game that could have been great but is held back by awkward gameplay design decisions, the start is fun but it gets very repetitive as you play, having to micro manage the drone is a chore and 100 floors was simply too much, had the game been simply 50 floors for the main story that would have been perfect, but if your someone who really likes roguelikes or arcade games then this game does have it's fun moments, but if you do decide to get the game then i recommend you get this game on sale, but as always, It's.. Up.. To.. You and i'll leave it at that.  (^_−).

its a good "turn your brain off" kind of game. the story is super simple, just your friend was captured by an evil person so you have to fight against endless enemies on 100 floors of a huge building. the game is a roguelike, so if you die or leave your session the format of the levels will randomize. you get materials for killing enemies and use them to strengthen your character to make the game overall easier.
the game can feel like a huge grind/slogfest the way it just drags. its best to play this game in bursts on something like the steam deck, i put most of my time in on my legion go s. i finished the game on my desktop tho.
other than that the game looks alright, doesnt run as good as it should considering how it looks but its a D3 game so im not too surprised by that. my biggest complaint is the final boss. its essentially three boss fights back to back with no refresh of healing items if you are out. and the final final boss is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of the boss teleporting all over the place and zooming everywhere. making them hard to shoot while they just hit and shoot you back to back.
if you like turn ur brain off games then get this, its not worth any more than like $12. problem is this game has NEVER been any less than like $35 on steam. i got this game through a humble bundle that contained this and like 5 or 6 other D3 games for about $27. the value of the bundle was probably almost $100 since these games are so overpriced.

I'm actually really liking this game.  It has a bit of fanservice and a very weird augmentation animation/character but its fairly minor in how its done in this game and is not so much that it overpowers the rest of the game.  I actually enjoy the livestream element of the game.  You get random challenges entering rooms from your chat and you can choose to make them harder for extra rewards, and just in general you see the chat coming up as you kick butt.  It's kind of like a style or score meter in other games.  At its core, the game is a 3rd person roguelite shooter with a tower with procedural generated areas.  You have persistent progression between attempts and random weapon and ability upgrades you get as you climb each time.  There are bosses at certain intervals and over time the enemy variety increases as well as the difficulty of the hazards/traps you see.  It seems like so far every 10 levels the design of the areas changes into a different sort of theme.  Overall, I'm enjoying it and will be completing this one.
